title: Junior Specialist: Full-Time Research Software Engineer

cond_0001.intro:
We are looking for a Research Software Engineer to join our team. The group is an interdisciplinary lab interested in exploring the mysteries of human, animal, and artificial vision, with a focus on the science behind bionic technologies that may one day restore useful vision to people living with incurable blindness.
We are looking for someone eager to contribute to open-source software solutions (C#/shaders, Python) and work with a multidisciplinary team of researchers to rapidly prototype and iterate on innovative ideas (virtual/augmented reality, computer vision, robotics) to advance the lab's research initiatives. This role is a good opportunity for those seeking to enrich their research experience (e.g., ""gap year""), aiming for co-authorship, and enhancing their publication record.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Develop and prototype software solutions to support the lab's diverse research initiatives, with the potential to contribute to publications.
Extend, enhance, and package our [Product name masked] simulator by developing new functionalities that contribute to our research.
Prototype novel assistive technology for people who are blind, working at the intersection of augmented reality and sensor-based technology, and crafting software for the analysis of multimodal data.
Maintain and improve our open-source packages, ensuring their effectiveness and reliability for research purposes.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
A BA/BS or current enrollment in an undergraduate degree in computer science, engineering, robotics, or a related field at the time of application; the degree must be completed by the start date.
Experience contributing to software development projects (e.g., C/C++/C#, Python, and/or CUDA/shaders), including participation in team environments or open-source initiatives.
Ability to work independently and comfortably in a multidisciplinary team; strong organization and problem-solving skills; attention to detail; good written and verbal communication; solid work ethic.
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with virtual or augmented reality platforms.
A demonstrated history of developing immersive virtual/augmented reality experiences.
A proven track record of contributing to production-level code in collaborative settings, including industry internships or open-source projects.
Experience writing software for integrated hardware components.
An interest in assistive technologies, neurotechnologies, and/or sight restoration.
cond_0001.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
cond_0001.values: We value responsibility, respect, and a genuine commitment to doing right by others. We aim to create outcomes that are fair, thoughtful, and beneficial to the people we serve.
cond_0001.inclusion: We seek candidates with a wide range of perspectives and backgrounds and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. [Company name masked] considers qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, sex, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

[Company name masked] invites applications for a research software engineer position. [Company name masked] is an interdisciplinary group interested in exploring the mysteries of human, animal, and artificial vision. Our passion lies in unraveling the science behind bionic technologies that may one day restore useful vision to people living with incurable blindness.
We are looking for a dynamic individual who is eager to contribute to open-source software solutions (C#/shaders, Python) and work with a multidisciplinary team of researchers to rapidly prototype and iterate on innovative ideas (virtual/augmented reality, computer vision, robotics) to advance the lab's research initiatives. This role is an excellent opportunity for those seeking to enrich their research experience (e.g., ""gap year""), aiming for co-authorship, and enhancing their publication record. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the kind of software and systems the work involves.
cond_0301.responsibilities:
Spearhead the development and prototyping of innovative software solutions to support [Company name masked]'s diverse research initiatives, with the potential to contribute to publications.
Extend, enhance, and package our [Product name masked] simulator by developing new functionalities that contribute to our groundbreaking research.
Engage in the prototyping of novel assistive technology for people who are blind, working at the intersection of augmented reality and sensor-based technology, and crafting software for the analysis of multimodal data.
Maintain and improve our open-source packages, ensuring their effectiveness and reliability for research purposes.
cond_0301.requirements:
A BA/BS or be enrolled in an undergraduate degree in computer science, engineering, robotics, or a related field is required at the time of application.
The undergraduate degree is required by the start date.
Experience contributing to software development projects (e.g., C/C++/C#, Python, and/or CUDA/shaders), including participation in team environments or open-source initiatives.
Familiarity with virtual or augmented reality platforms.
A demonstrated history of developing immersive virtual/augmented reality experiences.
A proven track record of contributing to production-level code in collaborative settings, including industry internships or open-source projects.
Experience writing software for integrated hardware components.
A keen interest in assistive technologies, neurotechnologies, and/or sight restoration.
The ability to work independently, efficiently, and comfortably in a multidisciplinary team environment; exceptional organization and problem-solving skills; attention to detail; excellent written and verbal communication; a strong work ethic.

The work centers on the science behind bionic technologies that may one day restore useful vision to people living with incurable blindness.
We are looking for someone who will take ownership of open-source software solutions (C#/shaders, Python) and drive rapid prototyping and iteration on innovative ideas (virtual/augmented reality, computer vision, robotics) alongside a multidisciplinary research team. This role suits those looking to build their research experience (e.g., ""gap year""), with opportunities for co-authorship and publication.
cond_0413.responsibilities:
Lead the development and prototyping of software solutions to advance [Company name masked]'s research initiatives, with the potential to contribute to publications.
Extend, enhance, and package the [Product name masked] simulator by delivering new functionalities that contribute to ongoing research.
Drive the prototyping of novel assistive technology for people who are blind, working at the intersection of augmented reality and sensor-based technology, and executing software for the analysis of multimodal data.
Own the maintenance and improvement of open-source packages, ensuring their effectiveness and reliability for research purposes.
cond_0413.requirements:
A BA/BS or current enrollment in an undergraduate degree in computer science, engineering, robotics, or a related field is required at the time of application.
The undergraduate degree is required by the start date.
Experience contributing to software development projects (e.g., C/C++/C#, Python, and/or CUDA/shaders), including participation in team environments or open-source initiatives.
Familiarity with virtual or augmented reality platforms.
A demonstrated history of developing immersive virtual/augmented reality experiences.
A proven track record of contributing to production-level code in collaborative settings, including industry internships or open-source projects.
Experience writing software for integrated hardware components.
A keen interest in assistive technologies, neurotechnologies, and/or sight restoration.
The ability to work independently, efficiently, and comfortably in a multidisciplinary team environment; exceptional organization and problem-solving skills; attention to detail; excellent written and verbal communication; a strong work ethic.

[Company name masked] is an interdisciplinary group focused on exploring questions in human, animal, and artificial vision. The work centers on the science behind bionic technologies that may one day restore useful vision to people living with incurable blindness.
We are looking for someone eager to contribute to open-source software solutions (C#/shaders, Python) and work alongside a multidisciplinary team of researchers to prototype and iterate on ideas spanning virtual/augmented reality, computer vision, and robotics. This role is a good fit for those looking to build research experience (e.g., a gap year), with opportunities for co-authorship and contributing to publications.
cond_0459.responsibilities:
Collaborate with the team on the development and prototyping of software solutions to support [Company name masked]'s research initiatives, with the potential to contribute to publications.
Work with colleagues to extend, enhance, and package the [Product name masked] simulator by developing new functionalities that support ongoing research.
Contribute to the prototyping of assistive technology for people who are blind, working at the intersection of augmented reality and sensor-based technology, and helping build software for the analysis of multimodal data.
Help maintain and improve shared open-source packages, ensuring their effectiveness and reliability for research use.
cond_0459.requirements:

A BA/BS in computer science, engineering, robotics, or a related field, or be enrolled in an undergraduate degree at the time of application (degree required by start date).
Experience contributing to software development projects (e.g., C/C++/C#, Python, and/or CUDA/shaders), including participation in team environments or open-source initiatives.
Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team; strong organization and problem-solving skills; attention to detail; good written and verbal communication; solid work ethic.

Familiarity with virtual or augmented reality platforms.
A demonstrated history of developing immersive virtual/augmented reality experiences.
A track record of contributing to production-level code in collaborative settings, including industry internships or open-source projects.

The group is an interdisciplinary lab interested in exploring the mysteries of human, animal, and artificial vision, with a focus on the science behind bionic technologies that may one day restore useful vision to people living with incurable blindness.
We are looking for someone eager to contribute to open-source software solutions (C#/shaders, Python) and work with a multidisciplinary team of researchers to rapidly prototype and iterate on innovative ideas (virtual/augmented reality, computer vision, robotics) to advance the lab's research initiatives. This role is a good opportunity for those seeking to enrich their research experience (e.g., ""gap year""), aiming for co-authorship, and enhancing their publication record.
cond_0595.responsibilities:
Develop and prototype software solutions to support the lab's diverse research initiatives, with the potential to contribute to publications.
Extend, enhance, and package our [Product name masked] simulator by developing new functionalities that contribute to our research.
Prototype novel assistive technology for people who are blind, working at the intersection of augmented reality and sensor-based technology, and crafting software for the analysis of multimodal data.
Maintain and improve our open-source packages, ensuring their effectiveness and reliability for research purposes.
cond_0595.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
A BA/BS or current enrollment in an undergraduate degree in computer science, engineering, robotics, or a related field at the time of application; the degree must be completed by the start date.
Experience contributing to software development projects (e.g., C/C++/C#, Python, and/or CUDA/shaders), including participation in team environments or open-source initiatives.
Ability to work independently and comfortably in a multidisciplinary team; strong organization and problem-solving skills; attention to detail; good written and verbal communication; solid work ethic.
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with virtual or augmented reality platforms.
A demonstrated history of developing immersive virtual/augmented reality experiences.
A proven track record of contributing to production-level code in collaborative settings, including industry internships or open-source projects.
Experience writing software for integrated hardware components.
An interest in assistive technologies, neurotechnologies, and/or sight restoration.
